data.name: Valeska
data.long_meaning: The name Valeska is derived from the Latin word 'valere', which means 'to be strong'. This name was used by the early Christians as a female form of the masculine name Valens, which also means 'strong' or 'powerful'. In Christian tradition, Valeska is associated with the strength and rule of God, and the call to follow His will.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the strength and rule of God, evoking a sense of faith and obedience.
data.numerology_meaning: Represents new beginnings, self-leadership and independence.

in_hebrew.name: ולסקה
in_hebrew.meaning: מקור גרמני, פירוש: חזקה, עז, חזק, סקה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ולסקה היא שם נשים יהודי, וכן שם משפחה, גרמני. פירוש השם: חזקה, עז, חזק. השם נכנס ללשון העברית כאשר יהודים גרמנים הגיעו ארצות הברית. בברית החדשה, ישנם בתים על חזקה. בתרבות יהודית, חזקה נחשבת לאחד החזקים. חזקה, כפי שנאמר, היא חזקה בכל תחומי חייה.

in_greek.name: Βαλέσκα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βαλέσκα είναι Γερμανικό. Η σημασία του είναι δυνατή, δυνατός. Το όνομα Βαλέσκα δεν αναφέρεται σε κανένα από τα κείμενα της Καινής Διαθήκης. Η παράδοση της Ανατολικής Ορθοδοξίας δεν αναφέρει το όνομα Βαλέσκα. Ωστόσο, η δυνατότητα και η αντοχή είναι χαρακτηριστικά που περιέχονται στη Βίβλο.

in_latin.name: Valeska
in_latin.meaning: Origine germanica, significato: forte, robusta, valente
in_latin.long_meaning: Il nome Valeska è di origine germanica e significa forte, robusta, valente. Non è presente nel Nuovo Testamento. La Chiesa Cattolica non menziona il nome Valeska. Tuttavia, la forza e la robustezza sono caratteristiche descritte nella Bibbia.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Valeska carries a strong spiritual significance for Christians. The name Valens, the masculine form, can be found in the Bible, specifically in the book of Philemon. The apostle Paul writes to Philemon, encouraging him to receive Onesimus, who had run away from slavery. Paul begins by addressing Philemon as "Valens", emphasizing his spiritual strength and leadership. The name Valeska, then, can be seen as a reminder of God's power and strength, as well as a call to follow His will.
